design_findings.finding: Detection rule fired on any single 15-min point; fixed (now needs a >= 1 h persistent period), regression tests added.
Time-of-day bias: the trailing 72 h baseline mixes all hours; elevated readings cluster 19-01 UTC and never occurred at 03 UTC in 40 days.
design_findings.reason: changes the signal's methodology; left for human decision. The sensitivity check shows it does not change the Event #15 result.

design_findings.finding: GDELT machine coding noise: e.g. a Nigerian article geocoded to Dubai and a Jordanian justice-ministry story coded CAMEO 190; verified in the raw rows, not a parser defect.
design_findings.reason: source property; recorded as a limitation

design_findings.finding: The 15-minute score is noisy (1 h autocorrelation 0.28).

event15.acceleration: corridor escalation events flat at ~40-80 per hour through the night; acceleration ratio at the event 0.90 (no build-up)
event15.breadth: broad Middle-East activity, not a single story: 1,307 corridor escalation events from 459 articles / 225 domains in the 24 h before; top article 1.4 %, top 10 articles 9.6 %
event15.categories_24h_before: armed_conflict 835, assault 157, threat 127, sanctions_reduction 63, coercion 50, force_posture 46, mass_violence 29
evidence_against: score 48 at the event, below the median at the 575 V1 timestamps (51.6)
the two pre-event elevated points (08:16, 08:46 UTC on 27 Sep) are isolated and occur at a ~2.9 % background rate
event15.lookahead_safe: yes: every score uses only batches available 15 min after their timestamp; events placed at DATEADDED
event15.regions_24h_before: Israel/Gaza 481, Iran 242, Yemen 89, US 66, Lebanon 57, Saudi Arabia 54 (ActionGeo country)
event15.scores_0100_0600_utc: range 16.5-65.5; no reading >= 90 from 2026-09-27T08:46Z until 2026-09-28T17:01Z (about 14 h after the event)

time_of_day_sensitivity.conclusion: the null result is not caused by the time-of-day bias
time_of_day_sensitivity.note: sensitivity check only, NOT adopted: same features against a same-clock-time baseline (previous 7 days, +/-60 min)

answers.broader_source_confirmation: yes in volume (225 domains), but not concentrated before the event
answers.information_v1_did_not_capture: different information, not shown to be relevant

incremental_value.event15_v1_gap: V1 had a 7.7 h observation gap across the event; GDELT had every 15-minute batch, but its reading in that gap was unremarkable

spearman_event_window_36h.note: small n; opposite sign to the full history

incremental_value.summary: GDELT carries different information from V1 geopolitics (near-zero rank correlation, keeps varying when V1 is saturated, continuous weekend coverage), but on this data that information did not detect Event #15 and did not lead V1's own sharp geopolitical moves. Different is not the same as useful.

limitations: GDELT has no ground truth; elevated periods are candidates, not labelled errors.
Export-file first-seen counts only (mentions table not used).

nature: Reviewed interpretation of the real-data run in gdelt_risk_regime_shock.json, for human review only. Not a V1 input, weight, confidence or methodology version.
recommendation_detail: Do not advance the current geo_shock_score: it did not detect Event #15 and showed no lead over V1. The source itself is not shown redundant, so a further research iteration (time-of-day normalised baseline decided in advance, more events, out-of-sample) is the only justified next step; otherwise reject.
